P0 is therefore competent-but-static: it trusts quoted MTBUR/TAT, ignores variability beyond Poisson and never re-plans from history.

assumptions.value: "total spares S = smallest S with P(Poisson(quoted annual removals x quoted pipeline days / 365) <= S - 1) >= protection level (95% D0, 90% D3/D10), i.e. the protection level is the probability that a demand finds a spare on the shelf (V2-SIM-10); quoted pipeline = quoted shop TAT + quoted vendor transit both ways + quoted core return weighted by the share rectified at an outstation (D0 50%, D3/D10 per the hub-deferral practice, wear-planned 0) (V2-SIM-11). Held at AUH (serviceable target = S minus the repair-loop units the run starts with), plus 1 outstation unit (line-station kit) for a D0 PN where the quoted station rate >= 4/yr."

limitations.title: The data is synthetic
limitations.detail: The airline, fleet, part numbers, removals, repair orders and AOG events are generated

limitations.title: Simulated rates are not reliability data
limitations.detail: MTBUR, NFF shares, condemnation rates and repair TATs are drawn from configured ranges

limitations.title: The models are tested on a world the author designed
limitations.detail: The generator draws removals from exposure ÷ MTBUR, which is exactly the structure the reliability-exposure forecast assumes

limitations.title: The vendor-quote error is assumed, and was set by the calibration
limitations.detail: The quoted MTBUR is truth × lognormal noise (σ_log 0.20) and 10% optimistic on average; quoted shop TAT is 5% optimistic (σ_log 0.10)

limitations.title: Demand is unconstrained and uncensored
limitations.detail: Every requirement is recorded whether or not stock existed

limitations.title: Two years of history
limitations.detail: Parts with very few removals cannot be forecast from their own history; they rely on the quoted MTBUR.

limitations.title: No exposure feedback from groundings
limitations.detail: A grounded aircraft keeps accruing its scheduled flying (protection by spare aircraft or sub-charter is assumed)

limitations.title: Rectification windows are simplified, not MEL
limitations.detail: D3 and D10 are simplified analogues of MEL repair-interval categories B and C, not operator MEL decisions

limitations.title: Brakes: cost-per-landing contracts are not modelled

limitations.title: The shop queue is light by construction
limitations.detail: A unit occupies a bench slot for only 5% of its work time (SIM-4), so shops almost never queue

limitations.title: Close to single-echelon
limitations.detail: Repairs happen only through the hub

limitations.title: Transport times are fixed planning values

limitations.title: Simplified scheduled maintenance
limitations.detail: Only A-checks at AUH generate kits

limitations.title: Parts are independent
limitations.detail: No interchangeability, no alternate part numbers, no next-higher-assembly logic, no common-cause failures.

limitations.title: Swaps and donors are simplified
limitations.detail: A borrowed or robbed unit is fitted at the requirement's station, and a robbed donor is assumed not to fly until it is reinstated from the next AUH unit.

limitations.title: The AOG cost is a scenario
limitations.detail: AED 15,000/h (narrowbody) or 30,000/h (widebody), plus a fixed AED 40,000 (NB) / 100,000 (WB) per merged event are planning values

limitations.title: Carrying cost is a single rate
limitations.detail: 20% per year (range 15–25%) covers capital cost, storage, insurance and obsolescence together.

limitations.title: The optimiser is a greedy heuristic on an analytic proxy
limitations.detail: Marginal analysis gives the best allocation only for separable, convex objectives at its breakpoints
